_comment: Hindu expansion 175-drive D: Brahmana ritual myths (Eggeling 1882/1885, public domain) and late-Vedic creation hymns.

title.en: The Severed Head of the Sacrifice (Pravargya)

region.zh: 俱盧-般遮羅祭地（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Shatapatha Brahmana 14.1.1, c. 8th-6th c. BCE (Eggeling translation, 1885)

source.archive: Internet Archive (Sacred Books of the East)
source.work: The Satapatha-Brahmana, trans. Julius Eggeling (SBE 44, 1885), Kanda XIV, Adhyaya I, Brahmana 1

summary.en: Once the Sacrifice itself was a person, Makha, with the gods for his retinue. Indra, asked for a share, refused, and struck off the sacrifice's head - which flew away and became the sun-like beast of the Pravargya rite, while Makha's body was spread into the sacrificial ground. Every altar-plan since is the map of a dismembered person.
summary.zh: 祭祀本身曾是一個人，名曰摩訶，諸神為其隨從。因陀羅索其份而不得，怒斬祭品之首——其首飛去，化為缽拉婆爾耶儀式中日狀之獸，而摩訶之軀被鋪為祭壇之地。此後每一祭壇的平面圖皆是一具被分屍之人的圖。

passages.text: The Sacrifice went in person, with the gods following; Indra, marching before, asked his share of the god-like victim, and being refused, smote off his head.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 14.1.1 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

passages.text: The head flew and became the glowing sun-like offering-vessel of the Pravargya - heated in the ritual every morning of the rite - the sacrifice's own head made a separate, sacred piece.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 14.1.1 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

passages.text: The body became the ground: each part of the altar maps a part of the sacrificed person, and the priest rebuilding the fire-altar each year is rebuilding the person of the sacrifice - dismemberment as blueprint.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 14.1.1 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

title.en: Narayana, the Man of a Hundred Heads

texts.period: Shatapatha Brahmana 13.6, c. 8th-6th c. BCE (Eggeling translation, 1885)

source.archive: Internet Archive (Sacred Books of the East)
source.work: The Satapatha-Brahmana, trans. Julius Eggeling (SBE 43-44, 1885), Kanda XIII, Adhyaya VI (the Purusha-Narayana sacrifice)

summary.en: The Brahmana's great sacrificial construction presents Purusha-Narayana, the cosmic man offered in effigy of a hundred heads, a thousand eyes - the ritual descendant of the Rigveda's sacrificed Purusha, and the first continuous appearance of the name Narayana, who will become Vishnu. The theology: whoever knows him knows the man in every man.
summary.zh: 梵書以百首千眼之祭形呈獻宇宙之人普魯沙-那羅延——梨俱吠陀被祭原人的儀式後裔，亦是『那羅延』之名的首次連續出現（其將成為毘濕奴）。其神學：知彼者，即知眾人中之此人。

passages.text: Purusha Narayana desired: may I encompass all beings; he created the all, and, offering himself in the sacrifice, became the first of the sacrifice's persons - a man of a hundred heads, a thousand eyes, a thousand feet.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 13.6 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

passages.text: The gods set him over everything: fire his mouth, the air his eye, the sun his heart, the directions his feet - the body extended over the cosmos in the same proportion as the altar.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 13.6 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

passages.text: Whoever knows this man in the sacrifice, says the Brahmana, knows the man in every man; the rite's effigy is the argument's diagram - and the name Narayana here begins its road to becoming Vishnu's own.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 13.6 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

title.en: Agni Hides in the Waters (Apam Napat)
title.zh: 阿耆尼藏於水中（阿波姆·那帕特）

region.en: Cosmic waters (symbolic pin at Pushkar lake)
region.zh: 宇宙之水（象徵性定位於布施伽爾湖）

source.work: The Hymns of the Rigveda, trans. Griffith (1896), Apam Napat hymns; The Satapatha-Brahmana, trans. Eggeling (1882), Kanda II

summary.en: Agni, the fire, once hid himself in the waters, afraid of the priesthood: the gods found him by his smoke, and the finding became the ritual of the new fire. In his waters-form he is Apam Napat, 'the child of the waters', a golden youth who shines inside the flood - fire in water, the paradox the tradition never stopped using.
summary.zh: 火神阿耆尼曾懼祭司職而藏於水中：諸神循其煙跡而得之，尋獲之儀遂成新火之禮。在水之形態中彼即阿波姆·那帕特，『水之子』，一個於洪流內發光的金色少年——水中的火，傳統無休止使用的悖論。

sensitivity.note: Ancient hymn and Brahmana ritual myth; classified 'myth'.

passages.text: Agni, when appointed priest, fled and hid in the waters: three times he was hidden, three times found; his smoke betrayed him, and the gods led him back to the altars with a rope of song.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda 10.45 and Shatapatha 2.2 (Griffith/Eggeling); not verbatim.

passages.text: In the waters he has another name: Apam Napat, the child of the waters, the golden youth at whose shining the waters smile - he sits at the bottom of the flood and lights the sky from below.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Rigveda Apam Napat hymns (Griffith 1896); not verbatim.

passages.text: The finding is ritual law: a new fire may be kindled only as Agni was found - by search, invitation and installation - so every household's hearth repeats the god's arrest and enthronement.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 2.2 (Eggeling 1882); not verbatim.

region.en: Kingdom of the performer (symbolic pin at Hastinapura)
region.zh: 行祭之王國（象徵性定位於象城）

texts.period: Shatapatha Brahmana 13.1-5, c. 8th-6th c. BCE (Eggeling translation, 1885)

source.archive: Internet Archive (Sacred Books of the East)
source.work: The Satapatha-Brahmana, trans. Julius Eggeling (SBE 44, 1885), Kanda XIII (the Ashvamedha)

summary.en: The greatest royal rite of the Vedic world: a consecrated stallion is freed to wander for a year, followed by the king's army; every land it enters must submit or fight. On its return it is sacrificed with the queen beside it in a ritual marriage of king, land and cosmos - the horse is Prajapati, and the year it walks is the year of the sacrifice.
summary.zh: 吠陀世界最宏大的王室祭儀：受冕的種馬被放行一年，由王之軍隊隨行；其入之境，或臣或戰。歸來後祭之，王后傍於其側，行王、土地與宇宙的儀式婚配——馬即生主，其行之一年即祭祀之年。

sensitivity.note: Ritual manual myth; classified 'myth'. Later epic Ashvamedha campaigns descend from this rite.

passages.text: The horse is consecrated with the words: this horse is the head of sacrifice, the king of the offering - then freed, guarded by a hundred young men, to wander where he will for a year, the king's rule measured in his footsteps.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 13.1-2 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

passages.text: The wandering is the empire's map: wherever he grazes unchallenged is tributary ground; where kings resist, the army that shadows him makes it a war of precedence.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 13.1-5 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

passages.text: At the year's end the horse is offered in a rite the Brahmana explains in cosmology: the horse is the year and the sun; the queen's part in the rite joins king, earth and heaven; and the sacrificer's sin of the year is said to be carried away by the victim - kingship bought with a cosmos in motion.
passages.note: Paraphrase of Shatapatha Brahmana 13.5 (Eggeling 1885); not verbatim.

title.en: The Riddle Hymn of the One Truth

region.zh: 旁遮普平原（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Rigveda, Book 1, Hymn 164, c. 1500-1200 BCE (Griffith translation, 1896)

source.work: The Hymns of the Rigveda, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1896), Book 1, Hymn 164 (Asyavamasya)

summary.en: Fifty-two riddle-verses on the wheel of order - the sun's seven-wheeled chariot, the seven mothers, the cow that drinks from her own hoof - ending in the tradition's most-quoted couplet: 'they call it Indra, Mitra, Varuna, Agni... that which is One the sages name by many names'. Philosophy hiding in a child's riddle-game.
summary.zh: 五十二節關於秩序之輪的謎語——七輪之日車、七母、自蹄而飲的母牛——終於傳統中引用最多的對句：『人們稱之為因陀羅、密多羅、伐樓那、阿耆尼……而智者以眾名呼那唯一者』。哲學藏於孩童的謎語遊戲之中。

passages.text: The riddles run on the sky-wheel: a chariot with one wheel, seven rims, driven by seven horses; seven sisters together spin a web, one spinning, another weaving, another arranging - the sun's year in a nursery game.

Deeper riddles follow: the mother at the top and the father below; the cow drinking from her own hoof-print; speech divided in four parts, three hidden and one spoken - the hymn teaching by a questioner who never answers.

The close resolves the game: that which is One, the sages call by many names; two birds, one eating, one watching, sit on the same tree - and the whole hymn is the oldest statement of the tradition's plural-name theology.

title.en: Aditi's Eight Sons and the Cast-Out Martanda
title.zh: 阿底提的八子與被逐的摩爾檀陀

region.zh: 旁遮普平原（象徵性定位）

texts.period: Rigveda, Book 10, Hymn 72, c. 1200-1000 BCE (Griffith translation, 1896)

source.work: The Hymns of the Rigveda, trans. R. T. H. Griffith (1896), Book 10, Hymn 72 (birth of the gods)

summary.en: Aditi, the boundless mother, bore eight sons: seven she presented to the gods - the Adityas - but the eighth, born a formless egg, she pushed away: Martanda, 'born from the dead egg', who was made the Sun instead. The hymn is the birth-registry of the gods, and the odd one out is the one who gives light to everyone.
summary.zh: 無邊之母阿底提生八子：七子獻予諸神——阿底多群——而第八子，生為無形之卵，被她推開：摩爾檀陀，『自死卵而生』，卻被立為太陽。此頌是諸神的出生名冊，而那個格格不入者，正是照亮萬人的那位。

passages.text: In the earliest age of the gods, Being was born from Non-being; then the regions of heaven were born, and Aditi, the mother of the gods, was born after them - or, the hymn jokes, the gods were born from Aditi; the parentage runs both ways.
Aditi bore eight sons: seven went to the gods; Martanda she bore the eighth, and cast him away from her - the eighth egg without a shape was not fit for the assembly.

With seven sons Aditi went to the earlier generation; but Martanda she brought forward again, and made him the Sun - so the cast-out one is the one who lightens the world: theology in a family's arithmetic.
